facts.detail: Ofcom lists current social-tariff prices ranging from £10 to £24.
Most listed tariffs provide unlimited superfast broadband above 30 Mbit/s.
Customers may switch to their provider's social tariff without a switching charge.
Social-tariff customers should not pay an early-exit fee.

guard_streams.write_limit: Price and account terms do not prove parcel availability, technology or speed.

facts.detail: Universal Credit claimants are included across available social tariffs.
Major providers also include Pension Credit, ESA, JSA and Income Support.
Some providers additionally accept PIP or Attendance Allowance.
The benefit recipient generally needs to be the main contract holder.

guard_streams.write_limit: Benefit eligibility is customer-account evidence and cannot establish parcel serviceability.

facts.detail: The programme ran from 31 October 2025 to 8 June 2026.
Regulated voice providers must take necessary measures for uninterrupted access to emergency organisations.
Providers must make accurate and reliable caller-location information available where technically feasible.
The obligations cover 999 and 112 emergency calls.

guard_streams.write_limit: Compliance duties do not prove parcel broadband coverage or local outage status.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom network and service resilience guidance

facts.detail: The resilience statement was last updated on 16 June 2026.
Guidance covers network architecture, design and operational models.
Ofcom notes outage consequences increase as society becomes more dependent on communications.
The guidance identifies resilience measures providers are expected to consider.

guard_streams.write_limit: Provider-level resilience practices are not evidence of uninterrupted service at a specific parcel.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom network security and resilience work

facts.detail: Ofcom has additional telecoms-security duties and powers since October 2022.
The framework sits under the Communications Act as amended by the Telecommunications Security Act 2021.
Public telecoms providers must identify and reduce security-compromise risks.
Providers must also prepare for security-compromise events.

guard_streams.write_limit: Security-framework compliance cannot be translated into parcel-level coverage or uptime.

facts.detail: The emergency video relay obligation came into force on 17 June 2022.
It applies to internet-access and qualifying number-based communications providers.
The service must be free and associated data zero-rated where technically feasible.
The approved service must be available 24/7 through compatible connected devices.

guard_streams.write_limit: Accessibility obligations do not establish broadband availability or performance at an address.

facts.detail: 999 BSL was the sole operating emergency video relay service in the evaluation.
The app had 26,632 downloads by February 2025.
Around 20,000 calls were made through the service in 2024.
The service provides equivalent emergency access for deaf BSL users.

guard_streams.write_limit: Service evaluation totals are national usage evidence, not parcel network measurements.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom text relay and disabled-services guidance

facts.detail: Text relay provides text-to-speech and speech-to-text through a relay assistant.
Landline and mobile providers must give eligible users access to an approved relay service.
Provider rules include priority fault repair for qualifying disabled customers.
Emergency SMS is available to registered hearing or speech-impaired users at no charge.

guard_streams.write_limit: Disabled-user services are protections and do not prove parcel coverage.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Bedfordshire Northamptonshire and Milton Keynes contract

facts.detail: The original CityFibre contract targeted around 25,000 premises for £51 million.
The original contract was signed in February 2024.
The May 2026 redesign reduced scope to around 6,000 premises backed by £19.8 million.
Detailed planning and physical build precede service, and premise scope may change.

guard_streams.write_limit: A redesigned contract is planning evidence, not current parcel orderability.

facts.detail: Gigaclear received two Oxfordshire contracts.
The combined contract value is £26.5 million.
The North and South Oxfordshire contracts target around 10,000 premises.
The contracts were signed in November 2023 and require build before service access.

guard_streams.write_limit: Contract awards and anticipated build do not prove present parcel availability.

facts.detail: Connect Fibre is the supplier for the Derbyshire regional contract.
The contract value is £33 million.
The contract targets more than 17,000 hard-to-reach premises.
It was signed in November 2023 and scope remains subject to planning and technical change.

guard_streams.write_limit: Regional procurement facts do not establish current parcel serviceability.

guard_streams.source: BDUK Cornwall and Isles of Scilly contract

facts.detail: Wildanet was awarded the Cornwall and Isles of Scilly contract.
The contract value is £41.2 million.
The contract targets around 16,800 hard-to-reach premises.
It was signed in April 2024 and requires detailed planning and construction before service.

guard_streams.write_limit: Award scope is not exact live parcel delivery evidence.

facts.detail: Openreach call-off seven covers Worcestershire.
The call-off value is £41.9 million.
The framework page records 22,600 contracted premises.
It was awarded on 19 December 2024 and requires preparatory build before service access.

guard_streams.write_limit: Framework call-off values and counts cannot identify parcel readiness.

guard_streams.source: BDUK July and May 2026 contract progress

facts.detail: The July release is a snapshot of data held on 16 July 2026.
The May release is a snapshot of data held on 21 May 2026.
The May release warns that supplier resubmissions reduced previously reported built counts for two contracts.
Both releases are initial-scope, rounded, lagged and not directly comparable with official statistics.

guard_streams.write_limit: Management snapshots cannot establish exact parcel delivery or contractual milestone compliance.
